title: Synchronous net-change mediation and slim-proofs PRD (draft)
body:
Overview

This draft PRD proposes a lightweight, synchronous mediation layer that runs during customer-managed VPC/network change windows and emits a compact, verifiable evidence packet ("slim-proof") for every materially observable change. The goal is to enable rapid approvals and auditability while minimizing telemetry volume and operator burden for both Redwood and the customer.

Context and motivation

We are seeing two opposing operational pressures: customers want low-friction, near-real-time network changes (eg: peering updates, NAT/gateway tweaks) during onboarding and normal ops; compliance/security groups want immutable, queryable evidence for every change that could affect inference connectivity or data paths. Current heavy-weight attestation approaches either: (a) flood telemetry and storage with raw traces, or (b) force slow, manual approvals. We need a middle ground that:
- preserves forensics useful for post-incident reconstruction,
- supports automated gating and SLA-aware rollbacks,
- is small enough to ship across constrained customer telemetry channels and low-bandwidth links, and
- integrates with Redwood Private’s approval policies and Console rollouts.

Problem statement

When a customer-operated network component that affects Redwood Private (eg. peering, route-table change, firewall rules affecting agent connectivity) is modified:
- Redwood needs high-confidence evidence that the change occurred and what the observable impact was (connectivity delta, affected tenants, timestamps).
- Customers want minimal friction for routine ops and predictable approval latency.
- Current designs either request full packet/flow captures (too heavy) or rely on sparse logs that are insufficient for auditors.

Goals

Primary goals (measurable):
- Produce a signed compact evidence artifact (slim-proof) per change that includes: change metadata, signed snapshot hashes (pre/post), minimal connectivity verification results, and a short operator statement. Artifact size target: <= 8KB gzip for common schema.
- Provide a synchronous mediation flow (can be bypassed with explicit policy) that runs in the change window and returns an approval token within SLA targets: 90% under 6s; 99% under 30s for routine changes.
- Support automated policy gating: e.g., deny if connectivity tests fail, or escalate to human approver.
- Index slim-proofs into Redwood Console audit timeline and make searchable by change ID, tenant, operator identity, and evidence tags.
- Allow customers to export slim-proofs to their SIEM or escrow store on a per-tenant or per-change policy.

Non-goals

- This PRD does not mandate full packet capture, full flow logs, or long-term raw telemetry retention.
- It does not change underlying cryptographic KMS choices for signature keys (we will integrate existing KMS APIs).

Scope and assumptions

In-scope:
- Change types: peering create/delete, route-table update, public IP reassignment, firewall rule modifications that affect Redwood agents.
- Evidence: pre/post compact JSON snapshot, connectivity probes (TCP/UDP handshake attempts), signed operator metadata, topology diffs.
- Mediation modes: synchronous (blocking until artifact issued and policy evaluated) and async (best-effort, when allowed by customer policy).
- Console UI: timeline entries, search, and manual download.

Out of scope:
- Full SIEM integration pipelines beyond export hooks (we add an export API but not full connector implementations).
- Customer onboarding workflows beyond initial opt-in flags and policy toggles.

User stories

- As a customer network operator, I want to make a routine NAT rule change without waiting 30+ minutes for approvals while still producing a signed slim-proof that my security team can query later.
- As a Redwood SRE oncall, I want to see a compact, verifiable artifact that shows whether a recent route-table change caused agent disconnects so I can triage quickly.
- As a compliance auditor, I want to be able to fetch the slim-proof for a specific change ID and validate the signatures and pre/post snapshots.
- As a Console user, I want to set a policy that blocks any change that increases the number of public-facing ports open to 0.0.0.0/0.

High-level design

1) Triggering and collection
- Change initiated by customer (CLI/Console/terraform). Change request includes operator identity and optional justification string.
- Redwood’s customer edge agent (or control-plane callback for hosted connectors) detects the change intent and triggers the mediation flow.

2) Mediation flow (synchronous path)
- Collect pre-change compact snapshot: small JSON describing relevant route entries, NAT mappings, and connectivity endpoints.
- Apply change (by customer or operator).
- Run minimal connectivity verification: a short set of probes (handshake to configured Redwood endpoints, tokenized API ping) that are timeboxed (default 3s).
- Collect post-change compact snapshot.
- Build slim-proof: {id, operator, timestamps, pre_hash, post_hash, probe_summary, policy_evaluation, signature}. Sign with Redwood edge key; optionally add customer-signed assertion if customer KMS is available.
- Evaluate configured policy (local predicates or policy service): allow/deny/escalate. Return approval token or blocking response.

3) Artifact lifecycle and storage
- Slim-proofs stored in compressed object store with retention policy determined by customer plan (default 90 days).
- Indexed metadata stored in Console DB for fast search. Full artifact available for download.
- Export API pushes slim-proofs to customer escrow endpoint with retry/backoff.

Policy examples and gating rules

- Soft gate: allow + record if probe failures are within tolerated bucket.
- Hard gate: deny and rollback if probe shows dropped connectivity to >X% of agents for >Y seconds.
- Human escalation: when change affects public ingress rules with open-ports to 0.0.0.0/0 or cross-account peering changes.

Telemetry and SLOs

- Mediation latency: capture times for snapshot collection, probe duration, signature creation, and policy eval. Dashboards: P50/P90/P99.
- Artifact size distribution (gzip). Goal: median <= 2.1KB, 95th <= 8KB.
- Success rates: signed artifact created vs. attempted (goal >= 99.5%).

Security and cryptographic considerations

- All slim-proofs are signed with Redwood edge key; design to optionally include a customer signature when the customer's edge connector can access their KMS.
- Support revocation/rotation: proofs include key id and signature algorithm; older proofs remain verifiable via published key history.

Console UX sketch (notes)

- Change timeline row shows: change id, operator, change type, pre/post topology thumbnails, small probe result icon (green/yellow/red), link to download slim-proof.
- Filter toolbar: change type, tenant, operator, time range, probe-status.

Rollout plan and milestones

- Phase 0 (experiment, 2 weeks): implement proof schema, local signature, and store; run in async-only mode for a single pilot customer.
- Phase 1 (pilot, 6 weeks): add synchronous mediation path for 2 pilot customers; instrument SLOs and Console timeline.
- Phase 2 (general availability): expose policy editor in Console, export API, and SLA-backed latency tiers for Dedicated/Private customers.

Acceptance criteria

- End-to-end pipeline creates and stores a slim-proof for every test change in pilot.
- Console search surface returns artifacts by change id and operator.
- Mediation latency meets SLA targets in 90/99 buckets in pilot.

Operational concerns and open questions

- Who bears signature key material when customer wants dual-signed proofs? (Legal + security input needed.)
- Retention policy variability by region/jurisdiction (GDPR/Schrems implications).
- Edge agent resource constraints: cost of probe traffic on constrained customer links. Need budget for probe throttling and adaptive backoff.

Risks

- Probe-induced outages in fragile networks if misconfigured. Mitigation: default conservative probe set, opt-in for aggressive probes.
- Customers decline sync path due to perceived added latency — we need easy policy to bypass.

Next steps (immediate)

- Schedule 1-hour design review with infra-security and legal (owner: Asha).
- Create Linear ticket for slim-proof schema (NET-432).
- Prototype small proof payload generator and sign verifier (owner: Miguel).

Notes to self (brain dump)

- Consider an "evidence brief" view that summarizes the important fields for humans (one-paragraph auto-summary).
- Could reuse parts of existing attestation code in control-plane; avoid redoing KMS plumbing.
- Keep schema intentionally minimal to encourage adoption.

References

- Related tickets: NET-432, NET-421
- GitHub infra PR with initial object store hooks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/789
- Slack thread: #private-onboarding (see pinned message from 2024-10-18)
